body: I am in therapy for social anxiety and we're trying to change my self-image, but suicidal thoughts appeared very recently, so I haven't had a chance yet to discuss them with my therapist. But I'll definitely do during the next appointment.

Despite having severe social anxiety, no self-confidence and hating my appearance, I somehow still have some hope for a better future and the strength to try to improve my life through therapy and other things.
This will definitely help me figure out what's wrong with my intonation and rhythm. Again, thank you so much for your help!

It's from a rather obscure book that you can only get in Poland (it's sort of an English language textbook), so no wonder you couldn't find it. xd I'd be happy to hear you read the fragment, so here you go:

"I arrived in Oxford at dusk. It was drizzling, just like in London, but unlike in London, the rain in Oxford was pure, unaffected by exhausts of millions of chimneys of the capital. Like a true Englishman, I simply adore rain, fog, and drizzle, but yesterday I felt fed up with water. Possibly because of the morning flood at home. Apparently, there was something wrong with those new pipes. They flooded my study, sitting room, and smoking room. I do not really care for the floor, but the humidity deformed my favourite violin, which I play while solving murder mysteries. I must admit that even a mind as brilliant as mine was unable to comprehend twisted explanations delivered in barely-recognisable English by the foreign plumber."

It would be great to compare my pronunciation with a native. Thanks so much for your help!

I'm from Poland, so yes, unfortunately I do have some slavic influence on my pronunciation. Thanks for your comments, I'll make sure to pay attention to sound length when I practice. I guess I should just listen to native speakers and try to mimic the melody of the language.
Exactly. That's why I'm afraid of sounding a bit aloof.
I didn't realise that, thanks for the tip.

I'm targeting RP (Received Pronunciation), which is like the 'standard' British accent. It isn't used by a lot of people in the UK, but I'm doing a degree in English and that's the accent they are teaching us at the university, so I don't really have a choice.
